author: Inside Edition
description: Melissa Rycroft, who appeared on "The Bachelor" and "Dancing With the Stars," made a lengthy apology after her second DWI arrest in 13 months. Rycroft was arrested on Saturday outside Dallas, hours after allegedly crashing her car into an ambulance and fleeing the scene. Rycroft was still on probation for her first arrest.
title: 'Bachelor' Star Melissa Rycroft Says She Needs Help After 2nd DWI Arrest

author: Inside Edition
description: The midterm elections were a night of many firsts. Georgia's governor-elect, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, will be the nation's first Black female governor. Amy Acton made history as the first woman governor of Ohio. New Hampshire elected the first openly gay man to the U.S. Senate, Democrat Chris Pappas. In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed will become the first Muslim senator in U.S. history. There were also big Democratic wins in Texas. Democrat James Talarico was elected Senator and Democrat Gina Hinojosa was elected governor.
title: A Midterm Elections For The History Books

author: Inside Edition
description: During last night's historic midterm election returns, a panel of political pundits at Politico had an idea: call President Trump to get his reaction to the "Blue Wave" sweeping the country. The president actually got on the phone. Inside Edition's Steven Fabian reports on the sea change in American politics, and what it means for Trump's presidency.
title: How Did Trump Respond To Yesterday's 'Blue Wave' Election Returns?

author: Inside Edition
description: The first midterm election results came in at around 6 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday. Very quickly, as state by state was announced, it became clear that what was initially called the "Blue Wave" had become a tsunami. Inside Edition's Ann Mercogliano has a timeline on how the historic night played out. In a lengthy social media post, Vice President J.D. Vance blamed the Iran war for the Democratic landslide.
title: How Midterm Election 'Blue Wave' Turned Into A Tsunami

author: Inside Edition
description: Veteran news anchors describe covering the midterm election results in real time as a major adrenaline rush. They often need that adrenaline, as well as lots of coffee and some cat naps to be on the air for more than 24 hours. Norah O'Donnell and Tony Dukopil kicked off CBS News' coverage along with Gayle King. Over at NBC, Savannah Guthrie was ready for round-the-clock duty. CNN's Kaitlan Collins geared up for a long on-air shift. O'Donnell shared a video diary of her long night.
title: News Anchors Pull All-Nighters To Cover Midterm Elections

author: Inside Edition
description: A humanoid robot shook hands and struck poses while out in public in California. The AI-powered robot was accompanied by a dog robot. Life-like robots made by a company called Faraday Future were sent out in public to mingle with and learn more about real people. However, there is a bit of robot backlash. A recent survey found 74% of Americans worry that robots will soon be taking jobs traditionally done by humans.
title: Life-Like Robots Meet People In Public

author: Inside Edition
description: Did North Korea pull off the biggest financial heist ever? A successful scam has a crypto company shelling out billions to its users and the FBI says hackers in the Hermit Kingdom are responsible. Binance says the cyber attack on their systems started in June, ultimately breaching employee computers and draining $6.3 billion worth of the currency from accounts. The company says it tried to freeze accounts when it realized they were under attack. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole $6.3 Billion In Cryptocurrency

author: Inside Edition
description: A woman who wanted to wear her mother's wedding dress for her own nuptials recently received a shocking disappointment. When she opened up the box thought to contain her mom's preserved gown, she found the wrong dress was inside. Inside Edition's Alison Hall has more on this wedding dress mixup, and the search for the right dress.
title: Bride Who Wanted To Wear Mom's Wedding Dress Shocked By Mixup

author: Inside Edition
description: Being a doctor came in handy last night. Physician Amy Acton had just begun her victory speech after her history-making win of the Ohio governor's race when alarming shouts went up from the crowd. The first woman elected to the Buckeye state's highest office abruptly stopped talking. “Someone passed out, we’re going to hold for a minute,” said Acton, who also is Ohio's former health director. And with that, she walked down to help.
title: Amy Acton Stops Victory Speech To Help Woman Who Fainted

author: Inside Edition
description: The people have voted and the mood is blue. Democrats captured key seats in the Senate and increased their numbers in the House, giving them control of both chambers come January. Not only did Democrats win their highly publicized Senate races in places like Texas and Michigan, candidates surprised the nation with victories in South Carolina, Iowa and Kansas. History was made for many governors-elect in states like Georgia and New Mexico. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Democrats Win Big In Midterm Elections Making History In Several States

author: Inside Edition
description: A child has died of measles in New York. It's the first reported measles fatality in 30 years, according to health officials. Specific details were not released, but medical experts are stressing the importance of getting vaccinated. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reports measles cases have doubled nationwide from last year. Outbreaks have been reported in 45 states and Washington DC. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: New York Reports 1st Child Measles Death In 30 Years

author: Inside Edition
description: A family of black bears in Tennessee broke into a truck for some munchies.
title: Bears Help Themselves To Beer, Snacks #shorts
